end.summary:
Practised ordering BCE and CE dates on a timeline.
Aarav correctly ordered 3000 BCE, 500 BCE, 100 CE, and 1947 CE.
They identified that BCE dates count down and CE dates count up from 1 CE.
Discussed archaeological remains, inscriptions, texts, and oral traditions as historical sources.
Aarav continued to say that one written source should be fully believed; this was not corrected by the end.
end.parentNote: Asha practised timeline ordering with BCE years counting down and CE years counting up. Aarav used the method to place dates in order and explained the direction of movement on the timeline. They also discussed why historians compare sources, including the example of a ruler praising themself, but the mix-up about trusting one written source was still present at the end. At home, ask Aarav to compare two short accounts of the same event and note one detail they share and one detail that differs.
